source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN Examination, 7th ed.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Twenty-four hours after a laryngectomy, bright red blood starts draining from the tracheostomy. What is the PRIORITY?
questions.rationale: A little bleeding right after surgery is expected and resolves within hours. Later bright red bleeding may mean a vessel is about to rupture, so the surgeon is notified.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q524 (PDF p. 720)
questions.quote: bleeding that is bright red may be a sign of impending rupture of a vessel.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A toddler has swallowed a household cleaner. Which action is appropriate?
options: Lay the child flat on the back
Call poison control and check ABCs
Give milk and wait for symptoms
questions.rationale: Poison control is called before other treatment. The nurse checks airway, breathing, and circulation, identifies the substance and amount, and saves any vomitus. Vomiting is not induced for corrosive cleaners.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q529 (PDF p. 727)
questions.quote: In the event of accidental poisoning, the poison control center is called before attempting any interventions.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with a C6 spinal cord injury in spinal shock is getting up to a chair. What should the nurse do?
options: Apply knee splints for the transfer
Teach locking the knees while pivoting
Raise the head gradually before rising
Stand him up quickly in one move
questions.rationale: Spinal shock often brings lower-limb vasodilation and a drop in BP on rising. A gradual increase in head elevation prevents dizziness and fainting.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q557 (PDF p. 758)
questions.quote: The nurse should provide for a gradual progression in head elevation

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: During a code, the physician about to defibrillate says loudly, 'CLEAR!' What should the nurse do immediately?
options: Step back from the client and bed
questions.rationale: For everyone's safety, all personnel stand back and avoid any contact with the client or bed when the shock is delivered.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q568 (PDF p. 773)
questions.quote: all personnel must stand back and be clear of all contact with the client or the client’s bed.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: What starting energy range is usually used for cardioversion with a monophasic defibrillator?
questions.rationale: Cardioversion, a synchronized countershock, usually starts at 50 to 100 joules, as prescribed. The higher ranges are too high for cardioversion.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q573 (PDF p. 778)
questions.quote: Cardioversion is usually started at 50 to 100 joules.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A spouse manages home IV lipid infusions. What should the spouse do FIRST if an adverse reaction is suspected?
questions.rationale: Signs of a lipid reaction include chest and back pain, chills, dyspnea, fever, flushing, and nausea. The priority is to stop the infusion to limit the reaction.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q712 (PDF p. 934)
questions.quote: The priority action is to stop the infusion to limit the adverse response.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A client hemorrhaging from a partial uterine inversion asks, 'What's happening? I'm bleeding. Am I dying?' What is she most likely experiencing?
questions.rationale: The unknown is the most common cause of fear, and loss of control causes anxiety. Her questions show fear rather than panic.
explanations: Requires knowing of an impending loss.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q901 (PDF p. 1144)
questions.quote: the unknown is the most common cause of fear.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: The family of a client in cardiogenic shock is very anxious. Which nursing action BEST supports them?
options: Insist they go home to sleep
questions.rationale: Flexible visiting hours reduce anxiety for both the client and the family. Insisting they leave is nontherapeutic.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q981 (PDF p. 1230)
questions.quote: The use of flexible visiting hours meets the needs of both the client and family for reducing the anxiety levels of both.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A ventilated client with respiratory failure is about to be weaned. Which comfort measure should now be LIMITED?
questions.rationale: Antianxiety drugs and opioids can suppress the respiratory drive and interfere with weaning. Distractions such as radio, TV, and family help with anxiety.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q985 (PDF p. 1234)
questions.quote: These medications may interfere with the weaning process by suppressing the respiratory drive.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Before IV insertion, a tense preoperative client says she does not understand why she needs an IV. What should the nurse say FIRST?
questions.rationale: Simple, clear information about the IV's purpose addresses her concern. Promising no pain is false, and dismissing her feelings blocks communication.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q991 (PDF p. 1241)
questions.quote: the nurse uses simple terms to clearly inform the client about the IV’s purpose.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with a new implanted chemotherapy port says, 'I can't handle a tube coming out of me.' What should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Explain the port sits under the skin
questions.rationale: An implanted port is under the skin, not visible, and has no external tubing except when accessed. Correcting this misunderstanding comes first.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q992 (PDF p. 1242)
questions.quote: An implanted port is subcutaneous; it is not visible, and it has no external tubing.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child with gastroenteritis is watched for hypovolemic shock. Which finding indicates COMPENSATED shock?
questions.rationale: In compensated shock the child becomes tachycardic to keep up cardiac output while BP stays normal. Capillary refill may exceed 2 seconds, and the child may become irritable.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1140 (PDF p. 1426)
questions.quote: In compensated shock, the child becomes tachycardic in an effort to increase the cardiac output. The blood pressure remains normal.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A ventilator's HIGH-pressure alarm sounds. Which is a possible cause?
questions.rationale: The high-pressure alarm sounds when peak pressure reaches the limit: kinked tubing, the client fighting the ventilator, secretions or a mucus plug, or the client biting the tube. Disconnection and cuff leaks trigger low-pressure alarms.
explanations: Not a cause of high pressure.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1245 (PDF p. 1538)
questions.quote: an increased amount of secretions in the airways or a mucous plug

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which action helps PREVENT ventilator-associated pneumonia?
questions.rationale: Intubation bypasses upper airway defenses. Prevention includes careful hand hygiene and keeping the head of the bed raised (30 to 45 degrees) to prevent aspiration.
explanations: Suctioning should be more frequent as needed.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1268 (PDF p. 1569)
questions.quote: Prevention includes effective hand washing before and after suctioning, when touching ventilator equipment

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with severe radiating chest pain is restless and dyspneic. Orders include oxygen at 4 L/min, cardiac enzymes, chest x-ray, and a 12-lead ECG. What should the nurse do FIRST?
questions.rationale: Oxygen comes first to limit damage from possible myocardial ischemia. The ECG and blood work follow shortly.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1278 (PDF p. 1579)
questions.quote: The first action would be to apply the oxygen because the client can be experiencing myocardial ischemia.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: IV 5% albumin is ordered for a burn client. Which history item should make the nurse call the prescriber first?
questions.rationale: Albumin, a blood derivative, is contraindicated in severe anemia, heart failure, renal insufficiency, allergic reaction, and when there is no albumin deficiency.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1295 (PDF p. 1596)
questions.quote: is contraindicated in severe anemia, cardiac failure, history of allergic reaction, renal insufficiency

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which PVC finding after antidysrhythmic therapy shows the treatment is INEFFECTIVE?
options: PVCs falling after the T wave
questions.rationale: PVCs are dangerous when frequent (over 6 per minute), in pairs, multifocal, or falling on the T wave. The provider is notified.
explanations: PVCs on the T wave are dangerous; after it is less concerning.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1299 (PDF p. 1600)
questions.quote: PVCs are considered dangerous when they are frequent (more than 6 per minute), occur in pairs or couplets, are multifocal (multiform), or fall on the T wave.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A ventilated client with a fat embolus is visibly anxious. What should the nurse do?
options: Ask family to stay at all times
questions.rationale: The nurse speaks calmly and reassures the anxious client. Asking family to stay constantly burdens them, and sleep does not relieve anxiety.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1512 (PDF p. 1822)
questions.quote: The nurse always speaks to the client calmly and provides reassurance to the anxious client.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with refractory myasthenia gravis asks why plasmapheresis is ordered. The nurse explains it will most likely:
questions.rationale: Plasmapheresis removes antibody-containing plasma proteins. In myasthenia gravis it is an adjunct that may give temporary relief, especially with impending respiratory failure. Usually 3 to 5 treatments are needed.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1525 (PDF p. 1835)
questions.quote: It is used as an adjunct therapy in myasthenia gravis and may give temporary relief to clients with actual or impending respiratory failure.
